newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRODEUR RECORDS LEAGUE-LEADING EIGHTH SHUTOUT FOR DEVILS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRODEUR RECORDS LEAGUE-LEADING EIGHTH SHUTOUT FOR DEVILS.

text.p: Martin Brodeur made 25 saves in recording his league-leading eighth shutout on Tuesday as the New Jersey Devils edged the Washington Capitals 1-0 to close within one point of first-place Philadelphia in the Eastern Conference playoff race.
Brodeur lowered his league-leading goals against average to 1.92 and limited an opponent to one goal or less for the 26th time this season in his 19th career shutout.

John MacLean scored the game's only goal at 7:20 of the first period. He took a pass from Brian Rolston and fired a one-timer past Bill Ranford from the inside edge of the right faceoff circle for his 24th goal.

Ranford made 26 saves for Washington, which suffered its third straight loss. The Capitals remain tied with Hartford for the final Eastern Conference playoff spot but Washington has five games remaining while the Whalers have seven.
Ranford kept the Caps in the game in the third period, but Washington could not solve Brodeur, who is 13-2-2 lifetime against the Capitals.
"We've had a lot of success against them," Brodeur said. "It's hard to explain. That's the way it is."

In Philadelphia, Rod Brind'Amour's powerplay goal at 10:10 of the third period lifted the Flyers into a 1-1 tie with the Tampa Bay Lightning, keeping them in sole possession of the top spot in the East.
Brind'Amour took a pass from Mikael Renberg at the right faceoff circle, moved toward the net and beat goaltender Daren Puppa between the pads with a wrist shot.
Chris Gratton gave Tampa Bay a 1-0 lead with his 27th goal at 2:56 of the second period.
Ron Hextall made 22 saves for Philadelphia. Puppa, playing just his fourth game of the season due to back surgery, made 32 saves for Tampa Bay.
In Phoenix, Craig Janney scored twice and added an assist and Keith Tkachuk had a goal and three assists as the Coyotes coasted to a 7-1 rout of the San Jose Sharks.
Jeremy Roenick and Cliff Ronning each added a goal and an assist for Phoenix, which is 8-3-2 in its last 13 games and tied for the fourth playoff spot in the West with Anaheim.
Nikolai Khabibulin stopped 32 shots in his 38th straight start and has allowed just seven goals in his last five games.
Ron Sutter scored 8:03 into the first period for San Jose, but the Coyotes tallied the next seven goals, including four in the third period off Sharks goalie Kelly Hrudey.
In New York, Esa Tikkanen's short-handed goal 6:28 into the third period lifted the Rangers to a 1-1 tie with the Buffalo Sabres.
Dominik Hasek held the Rangers scoreless through the first two periods, stopping all 24 shots, before Tikkanen's sixth goal of the season tied it.
Alexei Zhitnik scored midway through the second period for Buffalo, which ended a season-high four-game losing streak.

Hasek, playing his first game since March 17 due to a rib injury, finished with 37 saves. Mike Richter stopped 33 shots for New York, which moved into sole possession of fifth place in the East, one point ahead of idle Pittsburgh.
In Detroit, Tim Taylor's goal early in the second period lifted the Red Wings into a 1-1 tie with the St Louis Blues.
St Louis goaltender Grant Fuhr stopped a backhander by Joe Kocur but the puck landed in the crease and Taylor flipped it over Fuhr at 5:17 to end a 37-game goal scoring drought.
St Louis had grabbed a 1-0 lead on Pierre Turgeon's 26th goal at 7:32 of the opening period.
Fuhr finished with 24 saves for the Blues, while Mike Vernon stopped 20 shots in the Detroit goal.
In Anaheim, Steve Rucchin's powerplay goal with 11:17 left in the third period lifted the Mighty Ducks into a 3-3 tie with the Chicago Blackhawks.
Ruccin also assisted on the other two Ducks goals, including the 40th of the season by Paul Kariya.
Teemu Selanne returned to the Anaheim lineup after missing four games with a strained oblique muscle and had a pair of assists, giving him 100 points for the season.
Chris Chelios set up powerplay goals by Tony Amonte and Murray Craven for Chicago. Eric Daze also scored for the Blackhawks, who were outshot 38-29 and 5-1 in overtime.
